newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Sanevit share trading halted.
newsitem.headline: Romania Sanevit share trading halted.

text.p: The Bucharest stock exchange said on Thursday trading in syringe maker Sanevit SA would be halted next Tuesday pending a company annoucement on its latest shareholders' meeting.

The company requested that its shares not be traded on November 19 to give it time to inform investors of decisions reached by a general meeting of shareholders held on Thursday, a bourse statement said.
Sanevit, based in the Transylvanian town of Arad, was one of the six companies which opened trading on Bursa de Valori Bucuresti when it opened a year ago.
For the first few months, it was the investors' darling as the only private company on the floor and the sole manufacturer of disposable syringes in a country with a serious juvenile AIDS problem.
But interest in Sanevit has decreased gradually, with its price falling to a present 9,100 lei from an early 1995 peak of 71,000.
The bourse also said another nine companies -- including a dye producing company, a ship broker, a furniture maker and a pharmaceutical company -- had applied for a listing.
As many as 30 companies have applied for a quotation so far, but the exchange did not say when actual trading in their shares would start.
The bourse now trades 14 stocks. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
